title: Vaishnavism Saints Meerabai
definition: Meerabai (c. 1498–1546) was a 16th-century Rajput princess and mystic poet-saint of the Bhakti movement, renowned for her radical devotion (Bhakti) to Lord Krishna, transcending caste, gender, and social hierarchies.
importanceInUpsc: Essential for understanding the socio-religious reform movements in medieval India, the role of women in the Bhakti movement, and the evolution of vernacular literature (Brajbhasha/Rajasthani).
learningOutcomes: Master foundational concepts and mechanisms of Vaishnavism Saints Meerabai.
Evaluate spatial distribution, institutional frameworks, and policy dimensions.
Apply high-yield mnemonics to solve tricky Prelims and Mains questions.
prerequisites: Core foundational concepts of Saguna vs Nirguna Bhakti
